item.title: Liberation of Fiji Party wants new Constitution instead of amending 2013 Constitution
item.description: Fijians should have a completely new Constitution developed through genuine public consultation instead of making amendments to the 2013 Constitution. This has been revealed by Liberation of Fiji Party while presenting the party's submission to the Parliamentary Special Committee on the Constitution Amendment Bill.
item.content:encoded:
Fijians should have a completely new Constitution developed through genuine public consultation instead of making amendments to the 2013 Constitution.

This has been revealed by Liberation of Fiji Party while presenting the party's submission to the Parliamentary Special Committee on the Constitution Amendment Bill.

Liberation of Fiji Party General Secretary Manoa Malani says the party opposes the proposed amendments because questions surrounding the authorship, legal origins and democratic legitimacy of the 2013 Constitution remain unanswered.

Malani says Fijians deserve to know who drafted the 2013 Constitution, under whose authority it was prepared, who authorised its contents and whether the people were genuinely given the opportunity to examine, debate and approve it.

He says the party wants the authorship and legal origins of the Constitution to be independently investigated and publicly disclosed before another constitutional exercise is undertaken.

The party also raises concerns about the involvement of individuals in the secretariat responsible for Bill 32, and the Fiji Police Act 2026.

Malani calls for an independent investigation into what the party considers potential conflicts of interest and questions surrounding the handling of the bombing investigation.

During the presentation, Special Committee Member and Opposition MP Alvick Maharaj raises a procedural concern about Malani naming individuals who are not present before the committee to respond to the allegations.

Maharaj says parliamentary standing orders apply to committees and suggests that Malani refer to the individuals as members of the secretariat instead.

Malani says he wants the committee to understand the connections he believes exist between the different secretariat processes and why the party questions the neutrality of certain individuals.

The party's submission also calls for greater accountability, protection of human dignity, independence of institutions and proper legal safeguards .

It says immunity should never become a permanent shield against accountability, while justice must be administered through lawful procedures rather than political revenge.

The party further calls for all proposed legislative changes, including the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 and the Fiji Police Act 2026, to be made available in iTaukei and other languages to allow meaningful public examination and debate.

During questions, Special Committee Member Jone Usamate asks whether the party rejects everything in the proposed constitutional amendments and whether it has any suggestions for changes to the draft.

Malani says the party's concern is primarily about the process, including the need for comprehensive consultation and addressing questions surrounding the 2013 Constitution.

Party representative Marika Kalodama then clarifies that the party would prefer the Government to formulate a completely new Constitution rather than amend the existing one.

Special Committee Member and MP Praveen Bala also seeks clarification, asking whether the party supports amendments to the 2013 Constitution.

Kalodama responds that the party does not agree with the amendments and believes a new Constitution should be formulated.

Special Committee Member Sachida Nand then asks which document the party is referring to when it states that the people were not given a genuine opportunity to determine its legitimacy and contents.

Malani clarifies that the party is referring to the 2013 Constitution, saying this is why it wants an entirely new Constitution rather than amendments to the existing one.

Maharaj also questioned whether the party has conducted an analysis of how much of the 2013 Constitution is retained in Bill 32, including whether it has assessed the extent to which the existing Constitution is reflected in the proposed amendments.

Kalodama says the party's primary concern is trust, particularly because of the background to the 2006 events, the doctrine of necessity and the individuals involved in the development of the 2013 Constitution.

She says the party wants to start afresh with a Constitution that is built by the people and for the people, without being linked to particular institutions or individuals.

Kalodama describes a Constitution as a contract between the Government and the people, saying it should reflect the mandate of the people so every citizen can be proud of having been part of its development.

Nand then questions the party's position, pointing out that it wants the next election to proceed under the 2013 Constitution while also calling for an entirely new Constitution.

He says the existing Constitution provides for an amendment process and asks how the party believes a new Constitution can be achieved while relying on the 2013 Constitution to conduct the next election.

Kalodama responds by questioning why the issues surrounding the Constitution were not addressed two years ago adding, theÂ party is prepared to proceed with the 2013 Constitution for the next election and believes the incoming Government should address the outstanding issues after the election.

During further discussion, Special Committee members pointed out that the Supreme Court has ruled that the 2013 Constitution is lawful and valid.

Kalodama, however, argues that the Supreme Court's decision did not address the process through which the Constitution was developed.

She says the party's position is that the ruling concerned the legitimacy established through the three elections held under the Constitution rather than the process through which it was introduced.

item.title: NFA investigates fire at Kwong Tiy Plaza along Mark Street, Suva
item.description: Investigations are continuing into the cause of a fire that broke out at Kwong Tiy Plaza along Mark Street in Suva this morning. The fire, which was located in the building's Archives Room, was successfully extinguished by firefighters at 9.52am.
item.content:encoded:
Investigations are continuing into the cause of a fire that broke out at Kwong Tiy Plaza along Mark Street in Suva this morning.

The fire, which was located in the building's Archives Room, was successfully extinguished by firefighters at 9.52am.

The National Fire Authority says its National Command Centre received an alert through the Automatic Fire Extinguishing System at 8.01am, reporting a fire alarm activation at the premises.

Fire crews from Suva Fire Station immediately responded, with the first fire appliance arriving at the scene at 8.05am.

NFA says upon investigation, firefighters identified the fire in the Archives Room and immediately began firefighting operations.

The NFA says crews used the water supply from their appliance, with additional support from another NFA appliance and a nearby fire hydrant.

NFA Chief Executive Officer Puamau Sowane says the incident highlights how quickly fires can escalate, particularly in commercial buildings where offices, storage areas and important records are kept.

Sowane says although firefighters responded promptly and brought the fire under control, the incident could have had far more serious consequences, putting lives at risk, threatening neighbouring businesses and causing significant damage to property and important records.

He is urging businesses, commercial property owners and building occupants to remain vigilant and strengthen their fire safety measures.

The NFA is reminding businesses to ensure fire detection and suppression systems are regularly inspected and maintained, electrical systems are safe, and storage areas are kept clear of combustible materials.

They are also urging building occupants to keep emergency exits accessible, conduct regular fire drills and ensure appropriate firefighting equipment is available and serviced.

The Authority is further reminding the public never to ignore fire alarms, even when there are no visible signs of smoke or flames.

Anyone who suspects a fire should report it immediately by calling 910.

item.title: High Court adjourns King Khan’s legal and asset forfeiture cases until 20th January
item.description: The Suva High Court has adjourned proceedings till 20th January in the legal proceedings and asset forfeiture case brought by the Director of Public Prosecutions against Imran Khan, also known as King Khan. This is to allow Khan who is represented by Shayal Kant time to respond to the forfeiture matter.
item.content:encoded:
The Suva High Court has adjourned proceedings till 20th January in the legal proceedings and asset forfeiture case brought by the Director of Public Prosecutions against Imran Khan, also known as King Khan.

This is to allow Khan who is represented by Shayal Kant time to respond to the forfeiture matter.

Kant has been given 30 days to file and serve afterwhich the State will then have 30 days to reply.

The State is also seeking 21 days to respond to strikeout summons application filed by Khan's lawyer, then they will also get 21 days to reply to the State.

High Court Judge Justice Senileba Levaci has told the lawyers that they will also have the hearing on the forfeiture on the same day and written submissions are to be filed 7 days before 20th January for them to respond in court.

Justice Levaci also stated that they will also have the hearing on the stay application on the same day.

Earlier this year, the Suva High Court granted the State’s application for a permanent restraining order over the assets of Khan and Deborah Kim.

The Court declared the assets as unexplained wealth and ordered that they be permanently restrained after finding that the respondents had failed to provide evidence showing that the properties were acquired through lawful means.

The assets subject to the civil forfeiture application include $404,840.34 held in a bank account.

It also includes a three-bedroom concrete house and land at Lot 21 on DP 5225, Valelevu Housing Authority SubLease No. 204059.

Four vehicles are also covered by the application — a BMW sedan with registration FH 945, a Toyota wagon with registration KNGKHN, a Nissan sedan with registration 913, and a Toyota sedan with registration IV 991.
